top_problem: The grid measures clean (margins 12.7 mm on all four sides; item names at x 17.5 and 114.8 mm, 7 each; prices at right edges 101.1 and 198.4 mm, 7 each; all four cards sit on the 6 pt grid from the 126 pt deck origin; subheads and name bands match across each row). But the two cards in each row do not share an item baseline rhythm. In row 1 the second subheads land at y 127.0 and 124.88 mm, and from Manhattan down the item rows drift apart from the beer rows. El Barril also closes a gap of about 30 mm of dead space with an 84 pt filler foot. The boldest idea still missing is a true lotería tabla: every card built on one shared row module, so the list itself reads as a printed game board rather than four boxes with lists inside.
fixes: Put both cards of each row on one shared item-row module (for example 36 pt slots) so that Manhattan and Dry-Hopped IPA, and De la Casa and Sidra, sit on the same baselines across the gutter; y 127.0 vs 124.88 mm today.

Get rid of the roughly 84 pt empty well in El Barril by rebalancing row heights, or by moving content (such as the cider or a spirits subsection) into it, instead of filling it with the 'Nº 9 · EL BARRIL' foot.
Set the verse in the same place on every card face (same block width, same x and vertical centre as the figure): La Botella's single line and El Cantarito's three lines sit on different axes today.
Keep the card numerals (44, 41) inside the inner frame rule instead of crossing it, and pin them to the same inset baseline on all four cards.

Align the name-band glosses (Cocktails, Beer & Cider, Wine, Spirits) to one baseline with the caps, and use one fixed x relationship instead of letting each pair centre optically; headers now start at x 24.1, 127.1, 38.5 and 127.8 mm.

top_problem: The header system is measured-correct but flat. All four name bands are 7.67 mm tall at y 72.23 and 205.58, and the first subheads in each row match (84.67 / 84.67 and 218.02 / 218.02 mm). Subhead x is shared per column (17.46 / 114.83 mm), the band-to-first-subhead gap is 2.11 mm on every card, and the gap above each second subhead is 4.5 mm on three cards. So the hierarchy has only three steps: band name, 8.5 pt tracked subhead, 14 pt bold item name. The item names outweigh the subheads, so the subheads read as captions rather than section heads. The 'Cantina & Cocktail Bar' masthead is a generic sign above the tabla and does not belong to the Loteria system. The boldest missing idea is a masthead built as the Loteria tabla header itself, with the deck title set as the game's printed banner, so the page has one owned top level above the cards.
fixes: Make the subheads heavier than the item names. Set them at about 9.5-10 pt with a bolder weight or card-colour fill tabs so the order goes band, then subhead, then item, not band, then item, then subhead.
Recast the masthead as part of the Loteria concept, as a printed tabla banner with a card-style frame and the numeral motif, not a generic serif title under the papel picado.

Fill the 84 pt empty area and filler foot in El Barril with real content, such as a cider or draft note, or rebalance the row heights. The 'No 9 - EL BARRIL' foot reads as padding, not as a header-level device.

Put the English band labels ('Cocktails', 'Beer & Cider') on the same cap line as the Spanish name, or center them under it. Right now they sit baseline-low and off-center, which pushes each card name off the band's optical center differently (header x 24.12 / 127.08 / 38.54 / 127.84 mm).

Check the gap above DE LA CASA: it measures 8.74 mm from the last item name against 4.5 mm on the other cards. Confirm that the italic serve line is counted as the section's last line so the space above every subhead is the same.

Fill El Barril's roughly 84 pt empty foot with content, such as a michelada or an Iowa-brewed row in agave green, rather than a decorative rule, so the green card carries as much colour as the terracotta card.

lens: design concept and elevating elements vs the best bar menus in the country

top_problem: The lotería idea is signposted, not lived. These read as four coloured boxes with a small illustrated header strip and papel picado bunting, a festive Mexican trope seen in many restaurants. The missing bold idea is to make each section a real lotería card: a portrait, figure-dominant card with the number in the corner and the name in the bottom box, with the drinks list read as the tabla or cantor's call, all under a real venue name instead of the placeholder 'Cantina & Cocktail Bar'.
fixes: Make the lotería cards real: give each card face 50% or more of its card height with the figure as the hero, and move the number and name box to true lotería positions, so the concept, not the list box, is the first thing a guest sees.

Replace the generic papel picado bunting and the placeholder 'Cantina & Cocktail Bar' masthead with an ownable mark, such as a tabla-style masthead or a custom lotería 'La Cantina' card, so the page stops reading as stock festive trim.

Remove the 84 pt 'Nº 9 · EL BARRIL' filler foot by rebalancing the rows, for example by giving El Barril a taller face or a figure vignette, or by moving a short list up, so no card has a 30 mm dead zone beside the densest card.

Give cocktails, the high-margin category, more authority: a larger or featured house-original treatment (for example the Brown Butter Old Fashioned as a highlighted call-out), since four equal-weight rows on a cocktail bar menu undersell the bar.

Add one tactile texture layer, such as a cut-paper grain, card-stock speckle or registration offset on the figures, so the flat vector art gets the printed-lotería craft that Dead Rabbit or Pujol-level pieces carry.

top_problem: The lotería-tabla idea is only on the surface. It shows in the card faces and the name bands, but underneath each card is still an ordinary list, and the phone is the four print cards stacked in one column. Neither version uses what a lotería actually does: the cantor's call, the tabla you mark, the beans. That is the boldest idea still missing. It is also why the print El Barril card has a large filler foot, and why wine, beer and spirits read as bare lines ('Malbec · dry red', 'Cognac VSOP, poured straight.') next to the fuller cocktail card, on both paper and phone.
fixes: Fill the print El Barril card, or shrink it. Right now a thin rule and 'Nº 9 · EL BARRIL' sit in empty space about 50 mm tall under Dry Cider. The render script reports max_empty_space_in_a_card_pt as 0, which does not match the preview. Either give the beer and cider rows the same serve-cue line the cocktails have (glass or pour size) or rebalance the row heights, so the empty space gets a real use on paper as well as on the phone.

On the phone, widen the space around the stacked cards. The frames sit about 14 px from the screen edge while the text inside has about 40 px, so the 3 pt frames crowd the bezel. Give the outer margin the same share of the width as the 36 pt print margin, so the phone has the same breathing room as the letter page.

Give the lotería concept its own phone move instead of a scaled-down print page. For example, make each sticky chip a small version of its card face (number, figure, colour), or add a cantor-call line and a peek of the next card at the foot of each card as you scroll. Right now the phone is a faithful but passive single-column copy of print.

Make the four card faces follow one layout. La Botella's verse is one line set to the right, while the other three are two-line centred blocks. The card numbers are also squeezed into the frame corner (on the phone the '44' almost touches the frame). Give the number a clear inset and centre every verse the same way, so the four faces read as one deck in both versions.

Make the wine, beer and spirits descriptions as full as the cocktail ones, using the verified draft facts, so they no longer just repeat the item name ('Malbec · dry red', 'Brut rosé · dry sparkling'). Right now the lower two cards look unfinished next to El Cantarito on both paper and phone.

lens: every item and price vs the draft (build/draft_doc.json); descriptions, section flow and coherence for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City
top_problem: All 14 draft items are present with exact prices and nothing is invented, but nine of the 14 descriptions only repeat the item name with a style word: 'Malbec · dry red', 'Brut rosé · dry sparkling', 'Tequila blanco, poured straight.', 'Cognac VSOP, poured straight.'. None of them gives a region, ABV or age, so the beer, wine and spirit sections read like a placeholder list. The Manhattan also names only one modifier. On top of this, the tequila section (the cantina's signature category) sits last in the bottom-right corner, and El Barril has about 60 pt of dead space above a filler foot.
fixes: Get the flagged facts from the venue through the Coordinator (brewery, ABV, pour size; wine producer and region; tequila and cognac brand and age), then rewrite the beer, wine and spirit lines in guest language that does not repeat the item name. Until then, drop tautologies such as 'Malbec · dry red' and 'Tequila añejo, poured straight.' in favour of a style-only cue.

Label every wine price the same way: Brut Rosé prints a bare 13 under wine prices that say 'copa'. Either get its glass/bottle status (needs_input) and label it, or move the 'copa' label into the POR COPA subhead so no single price is left unlabelled. Also give La Botella's prices its card colour like the other three cards, instead of black ink.

Fix the flow: the Coordinator should push needs_input 7 (Mexican lager, mezcal, agua fresca) so the real items fill El Barril's 84 pt foot instead of empty space. If those items never come, rebalance the cards so the agave section is not the last thing read.

Remove the redundant text: the ' · draft' tag repeats the DE BARRIL · Draft subhead on all three beers, and 'AGAVE · Agave' and 'BRANDY · Brandy' are word-for-word pairs. Use one language for those subheads and put the space to better use.

Make the description style consistent: the beer, cider and wine tags have no end punctuation while the cocktail and spirit lines end with a full stop. Also get an answer to needs_input 11 so the Manhattan can name its bitters and meet the rule that a cocktail names its spirit plus two ingredients.

lens: ingredient names and description completeness vs build/draft_doc.json (honouring meta.public_components)
top_problem: Only the four cocktails have full descriptions. The other 10 items (beer, wine, cider, spirits) just repeat their name and category, with no ABV, region, grape detail or age. 'Malbec · dry red', 'Pinot Grigio · dry white', 'Brut rosé · dry sparkling', 'Tequila blanco, poured straight.' and 'Cognac VSOP, poured straight.' restate the item name. The gaps are honestly flagged in needs_input 2-6, but as printed, 10 of 14 items fall short of criterion 8. Checks passed: all 14 items and prices match the draft exactly (nothing invented, changed or dropped). Manhattan correctly leaves out the hidden aromatic bitters (flagged as needs_input 11). The Old Fashioned correctly prints its bitters. The cocktail serve cues come from the recipe_versions garnish/glassware data.
fixes: Rewrite the wine, spirit and beer lines so they don't repeat the item name, using only draft facts (e.g. Malbec: 'Dry red, by the glass.'; Blanco Tequila: 'Unaged, served neat.' only if the venue confirms), and print ABV, region and age as soon as the venue answers needs_input 2-6.
Give every description the same ending punctuation: cocktail and spirit lines end with a full stop, but beer, cider and wine lines ('Crisp pale lager · draft', 'Dry sparkling cider') don't.

Fill or rebalance the 84 pt empty foot on El Barril, for example by asking for a non-alcoholic agua fresca (needs_input 7 already asks). Also consider swapping La Botella into a prime top-row spot: an agave-led spirits card is the venue's signature for a Mexican cantina and should not sit in the weakest bottom-right slot.
Label Brut Rosé's price the same way as the other wines (copa or botella) once the venue answers needs_input 5, so that the wine card uses one price format instead of 'copa 12' next to a bare '13'.

Note in proposal.md that the order within subsections was changed from the draft (Margarita before Manhattan, Old Fashioned before Daiquiri, Cider merged into Beer) so the reordering is documented and not silent.

lens: flow and section order for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City
top_problem: For a cantina, the flow buries agave. Tequila sits in the last card (bottom-right, the dead corner), while El Barril top-right holds only 4 items plus about 60 pt of empty paper that a 'No 9 · EL BARRIL' filler foot pads out. The prime right-hand spot is spent on the weakest, emptiest category, and there is no non-alcoholic section at all.
problems: The draft has 14 items and all 14 prices match build/draft_doc.json exactly. Nothing is invented or dropped.

Section order is cocktails, beer & cider, wine, spirits. For a Mexican cantina, agave is the house identity and should sit next to or directly under the cocktails, not last. The designer says agave_top does not fit the 630 pt deck, but that is a layout constraint and does not justify the reading order.
El Barril has about 60 pt of dead space between Dry Cider and the foot rule. The foot line repeats the card name and number already printed on the face, so it is filler, not content.
There is no non-alcoholic or agua fresca section, which a Mexican restaurant in a college town is expected to have. It is flagged as needs_input 7 in proposal.md but not on the menu.
Glass/bottle labels are inconsistent. Malbec and Pinot Grigio carry 'copa' but Brut Rosé under ESPUMOSO has none, so its serve size is unlabelled.

Beer has no ABV and wine has no region: 'Malbec · dry red' and 'Pinot Grigio · dry white' repeat the item name as the grape. These are flagged in proposal.md as missing, which is correct, but the printed descriptions are thin.
Spirits descriptions just repeat the item name ('Tequila blanco, poured straight.' under 'Blanco Tequila'). They add no type or age information beyond the name.
The Manhattan names only rye and sweet vermouth because the draft hides the bitters (public_components flag), so it fails the spirit-plus-two-ingredients check. It is flagged as needs_input 11.
The bilingual subheads 'AGAVE · Agave' and 'BRANDY · Brandy' repeat the same word, so the SPANISH · English system becomes noise in those two cards.
fixes: Restructure so agave sits in the prime right-hand slot beside El Cantarito. Examples: make the top row 'El Cantarito | La Botella' and resolve the height mismatch by moving Beer & Cider and Wine into the lower row, or fold Agave into the cocktail card as a 'Tequila & Mezcal' strip.
Remove the El Barril filler foot. Fill that space with real items only after the venue answers needs_input 7 (additional beers or agua fresca), or rebalance rows so no card needs padding.
Add 'copa' or 'botella' (whichever the venue confirms) to Brut Rosé so every wine price carries the same serve label as the other two.

Get ABV for each beer and a region for each wine from the venue and print them (for example 'Czech-style pilsner · 4.8% · draft'). Until then, show the missing_ingredients flags rather than style tags that restate the name.

Replace the redundant 'AGAVE · Agave' and 'BRANDY · Brandy' subheads with one-language labels or real Spanish/English pairs, and get the venue to confirm the Manhattan bitters so the classic reads spirit plus two modifiers.

top_problem: The copy has no single voice. Only the Margarita gets a flavour lead ('Bright and citrus-forward:'); the other cocktails open with a bare method ('Stirred:', 'Shaken:'). Beer, wine and spirits read like database tags that repeat the item name ('Malbec · dry red', 'Pinot Grigio · dry white', 'Tequila blanco, poured straight.' under 'Blanco Tequila'). Beer has no ABV, wine has no region and spirits have no age or brand, and none of these gaps is flagged on the page. So a strong lotería concept carries list copy that sounds like a spreadsheet next to the cantor verses.
fixes: Use one cocktail pattern on every drink: method lead + spirit + modifiers, then the serve cue. The Margarita should open with its sourced method, like the Manhattan, Old Fashioned and Daiquiri. If the flavour note 'Bright and citrus-forward' stays, give every cocktail a sourced flavour note or cut it.

Rewrite beer, wine and spirit lines so they don't repeat the item name: 'Malbec · dry red' becomes 'Dry red · [region]'; 'Tequila blanco, poured straight' becomes 'Unaged · poured neat' or the agave/brand. Record every missing ABV, region, age and brand as a missing_ingredients / needs_input question, and don't print a line that only repeats the name.
Label the Brut Rosé price as 'copa' (or 'botella') like the other two wines, so every wine price in La Rosa has a pour label.

Fill El Barril's 84 pt empty foot with real items (the needs_input 7 beer, cider or agua fresca) or a non-alcoholic card, not the filler line 'Nº 9 · EL BARRIL'. A cantina menu also needs a sin alcohol section to be complete.

Drop the gloss when it only repeats the Spanish ('AGAVE · Agave', 'BRANDY · Brandy'), or use 'AGAVE · Tequila' and 'BRANDY · Coñac'. Also match item-name word order to the description: 'Blanco Tequila' vs 'Tequila blanco'.

lens: how missing data is handled and flagged (draft: ../build/draft_doc.json)
top_problem: The unknowns are only flagged in proposal.md prose. Every missing_ingredients array in round-16/doc.json is empty, even though needs_input 6 says the spirits are 'flagged in missing_ingredients'. On the printed menu the gaps show up as thin filler text instead of a clear marker: the beers have no ABV ('Crisp pale lager · draft'), the wines have no region and only repeat their names ('Malbec · dry red'), the spirits have no age or brand ('Tequila blanco, poured straight.'), and the Brut Rosé price has no label. All 14 item prices match the draft exactly, and nothing was invented or dropped.
fixes: Fill missing_ingredients in doc.json for every item that has a gap: ABV, brewery and pour size for the 3 beers and the cider; region, producer and vintage for Malbec, Pinot Grigio and Brut Rosé; brand, age and pour size for Blanco Tequila, Añejo Tequila and Cognac VSOP; bitters visibility for the Manhattan. The machine-readable flag then matches needs_input 2-6 and 11.

Until the venue supplies region and style, rewrite the wine descriptions so they stop repeating the item name ('Malbec · dry red', 'Pinot Grigio · dry white', 'Brut rosé · dry sparkling'). Use only known facts, such as the grape and style, plus a visible 'region to come' placeholder in the proof copy, and do not make up origins.

Give the Brut Rosé price the same label style as the other wines ('copa' like Malbec and Pinot Grigio, or 'botella'), or hold the item out of the print proof until needs_input 5 is answered. An unlabelled wine price next to labelled 'copa' prices breaks the price format.

Drop the repeated subheads 'Agave · Agave' and 'Brandy · Brandy': print only the Spanish word, or add an English gloss that says something new. Then use the 84 pt empty foot in El Barril for a non-alcoholic or Mexican-lager slot once needs_input 7 and 12 are answered, not for filler.

Add a short proof-only marker, such as a small dagger with a footnote 'details pending from venue', beside each item whose ingredient data is incomplete. Reviewers and the venue can then see the gaps on the preview, while the guest version stays clean.

lens: Trace printed ingredients, garnishes, glassware, serve, method leads and subhead labels to their sources (gateway log_id 197: phg.menu_items joined to phg.recipe_versions on current_recipe_version_id; draft snapshot build/draft_doc.json)
top_problem: Most cocktail facts check out, but the three spirits print a serve, 'poured straight', that nothing in the data supports. On top of that, the wine and spirit lines mostly repeat the item name ('Malbec · dry red', 'Tequila blanco, poured straight.'), so half the menu reads like a classification label, not guest copy.
verified: Margarita: 'tequila blanco, fresh lime, orange liqueur and agave syrup' matches the draft components (Tequila Blanco, Fresh Lime Juice, Orange Liqueur, Agave Syrup). 'Bright and citrus-forward' is from menu_items.menu_description. 'On the rocks, lime wheel' matches recipe_versions f06abb74: glassware Rocks, method 'Shake with ice and strain over fresh ice', garnish 'Lime wheel'. OK.

Manhattan: 'Stirred:' matches rv 9fb77eaa method 'Stir with ice and strain'. 'In a coupe, cocktail cherry' matches glassware Coupe and garnish 'Cocktail cherry'. Aromatic bitters are correctly left off because the draft has meta.public_components {'aromatic-bitters': false}. OK.

Brown Butter Old Fashioned: 'Stirred:' and 'Over a large cube' match rv 7095fd3d method 'Stir with ice and strain over a large cube'. 'Orange peel' matches its garnish. The ingredients match the draft components verbatim. OK.

House Daiquiri: 'Shaken:' matches rv 14d45e57 method 'Shake with ice and fine strain'. 'In a coupe, lime coin' matches glassware Coupe and garnish 'Lime coin'. 'House demerara syrup' matches the component note 'House 1:1 demerara syrup'. OK.
Beer, wine and cider style words (crisp pale lager, hop-forward IPA, toasty amber lager, dry red, dry white, dry sparkling, dry sparkling cider) all match menu_items.menu_description. OK.
All 14 printed prices match menu_items.menu_price. OK.
The loteria numbers and verses are correct Don Clemente: El Cantarito 44, El Barril 9, La Rosa 41, La Botella 8. Accents are correct (cántaro, bebió, albañil, quedó). OK.
problems: Criterion 11: 'poured straight' on Blanco Tequila, Añejo Tequila and Cognac VSOP has no source. recipe_versions method, glassware and garnish are null for all three, and menu_description only says 'Blanco tequila pour.', 'Añejo tequila pour.' and 'VSOP Cognac pour.'. 'Straight' is an invented serve fact, since the venue may pour neat, on the rocks or with sangrita.

Criterion 11 (minor): the Margarita's 'On the rocks' reads 'Rocks' glassware as an ice style. The method 'strain over fresh ice' supports it, so it is acceptable, but the proposal should cite the method row, not only the glassware.

Criterion 12: Malbec 'Malbec · dry red', Pinot Grigio 'Pinot Grigio · dry white' and Brut Rosé 'Brut rosé · dry sparkling' each open by repeating the item name. The spirit lines do the same ('Tequila blanco…', 'Cognac VSOP…'). Beer lines tack on '· draft' directly under a 'DE BARRIL · Draft' subhead. These are taxonomy strings, not guest language.

Criterion 12: the voice changes between cards. Cocktails use 'Lead: ingredients.' plus an italic serve line, beer and wine use 'style · tag' fragments, and spirits use sentences. The Manhattan line 'Stirred: rye, sweet vermouth.' reads clipped with no sensory word, while the Margarita gets one.

Criterion 13: the subheads 'AGAVE · Agave' and 'BRANDY · Brandy' print the same word twice, which looks like a bug rather than a bilingual pair. The draft sub names support Agave and Brandy, but the doubled pair wastes the Spanish device used everywhere else.

Criterion 13: the masthead 'Cantina & Cocktail Bar' is generic, and nothing beyond the Margarita and the tequilas speaks to a Mexican restaurant; that is a limit of the item list, not the copy. The loteria system and Spanish subheads carry the venue well. I did not run a census/ZCTA check within the 2-query budget.
Criterion 14: El Barril has about 60 mm of dead space between Dry Cider and its 'Nº 9 · EL BARRIL' foot, so the card reads half empty next to a full El Cantarito.

Criterion 14: 'copa' price labels print on Malbec and Pinot Grigio, but Brut Rosé's 13 is unlabelled in the same card. That is consistent with the draft (empty label), but a guest cannot tell whether it is a glass or a bottle.

Criterion 14: in El Cantarito, cocktail descriptions break well short of the price column ('Shaken: white rum, fresh lime and / house demerara syrup.'), which leaves ragged, widowed second lines. Each cocktail runs to three lines where two would fit at the full measure.

Criterion 13 / content: phg.menu_items has a 15th row, Junmai Ginjo ($12, 'Junmai Ginjo sake.'), that is not printed and not in the draft snapshot's subs. The Content reviewer should confirm whether leaving it off was intended.
fixes: Remove 'poured straight' from the three spirits (method, glassware and garnish are null in phg.recipe_versions for them) and print only sourced words, for example 'Blanco · tequila pour', or flag serve style as missing_ingredients.

Rewrite the wine, spirit and beer lines so they do not open with the item name, using only menu_description words (for example Malbec: 'Dry and red'; Brut Rosé: 'Dry sparkling rosé'), and drop the redundant '· draft' under the De Barril subhead.
Replace the doubled 'AGAVE · Agave' and 'BRANDY · Brandy' with one word or a real Spanish/English pair, and add a sourced sensory word to the Manhattan so all four cocktails share one voice.
Layout note for the designer: widen the cocktail description measure to the price column's left edge so each cocktail sits on two lines, and fill or rebalance the empty lower half of El Barril.
Flag Brut Rosé's glass or bottle status on the menu itself (or get the label from the venue) so it matches the 'copa' labels on the other wine prices.

lens: description quality and one guest voice
top_problem: 9 of the 14 descriptions just repeat the item name in a tag or class format: 'Malbec · dry red', 'Pinot Grigio · dry white', 'Brut rosé · dry sparkling', 'Dry sparkling cider', 'Hop-forward IPA · draft', 'Toasty amber lager · draft', 'Tequila blanco, poured straight.', 'Tequila añejo, poured straight.', 'Cognac VSOP, poured straight.' That is the criterion-12 auto-fail pattern. The menu also uses three voices: recipe-card cocktails ('Stirred: …'), dot tags on beer and wine, and flat sentences on spirits. The lotería concept does not reach the copy. What I verified: every cocktail garnish, glass and method traces to phg.recipe_versions (Margarita f06abb74: Rocks / Lime wheel / shaken over fresh ice; Manhattan 9fb77eaa: Coupe / Cocktail cherry / stirred; House Daiquiri 14d45e57: Coupe / Lime coin / shaken; Brown Butter Old Fashioned 7095fd3d: Rocks / Orange peel / stirred over a large cube). Beer, wine, cider and spirits have no recipe_version, so the only facts they can print are the draft_doc descriptions. The Manhattan drops 'aromatic bitters', which the draft description lists (draft_doc beta_manhattan). The four lotería verses and card numbers are correct.
fixes: Rewrite the 9 name-echo descriptions into one sensory guest voice using only the draft facts (for example Czech Pilsner 'Crisp and clean, a pale lager poured from the tap'; Malbec 'A dry red, deep and generous'), and drop the '· draft' tags because the 'De Barril' header already says it.

Give one lead-in pattern to all four cocktails: the Margarita opens with 'Bright and citrus-forward:' while the other three open with a method ('Stirred:' / 'Shaken:'); either give all of them a flavour lead or open the Margarita with 'Shaken:' (recipe_versions f06abb74 method).

Restore 'aromatic bitters' to the Manhattan (draft_doc beta_manhattan 'Rye, sweet vermouth, aromatic bitters.') unless public_components marks it hidden; right now the Manhattan is the thinnest cocktail line on the page.

Fix the doubled bilingual subheads 'Agave · Agave' and 'Brandy · Brandy' (use 'Agave' alone or 'Destilados de Agave · Agave', and 'Coñac · Brandy'), and put the 'copa' pour label on the Brut Rosé as well so all wine prices carry the same label.

Layout note for the designer: the El Barril card has about 1.5 inches of dead space above its footer, and the Daiquiri line breaks early ('fresh lime and / house demerara syrup'); fuller beer and cider descriptions would fill the card and balance it against El Cantarito.

lens: venue-type fit: Mexican cantina and cocktail bar in Iowa City (ZIP 52240), Spanish and loteria usage including verses
top_problem: The loteria concept is correct and well sourced. The four Don Clemente numbers (El Cantarito 44, El Barril 9, La Rosa 41, La Botella 8) and all four cantor verses are the traditional ones, spelled correctly. The problem is the menu under the concept. The agave card is last in reading order (bottom right). Only 1 of 4 cocktails is agave-based. The subheads repeat the same word in both languages (AGAVE · Agave, BRANDY · Brandy). The non-cocktail descriptions are 'style · serve' tags that restate the item name (Malbec · dry red, Pinot Grigio · dry white, Tequila blanco, poured straight). So the text inside the cards reads like a generic bar list in cantina costume. The design is also missing its single boldest move: making agave the cantina's lead card instead of the last one.
verified: Margarita: 'On the rocks, lime wheel' and 'fresh lime, orange liqueur and agave syrup' come from recipe_versions f06abb74 (glassware Rocks, garnish Lime wheel, method Shake with ice and strain over fresh ice) and the draft components Tequila Blanco, Fresh Lime Juice, Orange Liqueur, Agave Syrup. The lead 'Bright and citrus-forward' is from the draft desc.

Manhattan: 'Stirred', 'In a coupe, cocktail cherry' come from rv 9fb77eaa (Coupe, Cocktail cherry, Stir with ice and strain). The bitters are left out correctly, because draft meta.public_components has aromatic-bitters set to false.

Brown Butter Old Fashioned: 'Over a large cube, orange peel' comes from rv 7095fd3d (Rocks, Orange peel, Stir with ice and strain over a large cube). The components Brown Butter-Washed Bourbon, Demerara Syrup and Aromatic Bitters match the draft.
House Daiquiri: 'Shaken', 'In a coupe, lime coin' and 'house demerara syrup' come from rv 14d45e57 (Coupe, Lime coin, Shake with ice and fine strain) and the draft desc.

Beer, wine and spirits tags match the draft descs (Crisp pale lager, Hop-forward draft IPA, Toasty amber lager, Dry red wine, Dry white wine, Dry sparkling rosé, Blanco/Añejo tequila pour, VSOP Cognac pour) and the spirits section desc 'Straight pours by category.' 'copa' is inferred from the draft sub 'By the Glass', because the draft price labels are empty. That inference is acceptable, but it has no row of its own.

phg_census_zcta 52240: median age 28.6, 29.9% aged 21 to 34, median household income $52,960, 26.1% of households over $100k, 47.6% with a bachelor's degree or higher, 11.0% Hispanic or Latino. This is a college-town crowd. $14 to $16 cocktails are the top of the local tier, and $7 to $8 drafts fit it.
problems: 13: Agave, the category that defines a cantina, is on the last card (La Botella, bottom right) and has only 2 pours. The proposal says the agave-top order needs 660 pt against a 630 pt deck, but that is a layout constraint. It is not a venue reason for leaving the cantina's signature category last.

13: The bilingual subheads are uneven. CLÁSICOS · Classics, DE BARRIL · Draft and POR COPA · By the Glass are good Spanish. AGAVE · Agave and BRANDY · Brandy repeat the same word, which reads as filler. BRANDY could be COÑAC, which matches the only item, but that needs the Coordinator's sign-off because the draft sub name is 'Brandy'.
13: The masthead 'Cantina & Cocktail Bar / IOWA CITY, IOWA' carries no venue name or voice. The title is generic, so the menu could belong to any Midwest Mexican-themed bar.

13: The draft has no Mexican lager, michelada, mezcal or agua fresca, and no non-alcoholic section at all, although this crowd (median age 28.6) would expect them. This is a draft gap, not a designer error, but the proposal should flag it more clearly than needs_input 7.

12: The non-cocktail lines are tags, not guest language. 'Malbec · dry red', 'Pinot Grigio · dry white', 'Brut rosé · dry sparkling' and 'Tequila blanco, poured straight' / 'Tequila añejo, poured straight' mostly restate the item name, and 'poured straight' is taxonomy wording taken from the section desc. That gives two voices, full sentences for cocktails and data tags for everything else.
12: The Manhattan's 'Stirred: rye, sweet vermouth.' is thin next to the other cocktails. With the bitters hidden it reads unfinished.

14: El Barril has an 84 pt foot and about 60 pt of empty cream between Dry Cider and the 'Nº 9 · EL BARRIL' rule. That is the one visibly under-filled area, and the orphaned foot line looks like padding.

14: Brut Rosé under ESPUMOSO has no serve label, while the two POR COPA wines carry 'copa'. The draft section desc says 'by the glass and sparkling selections', so a guest cannot tell whether $13 buys a glass or a bottle.
fixes: Ask the Coordinator or venue for 1 to 2 more agave pours or an agave cocktail, and for a Mexican lager or agua fresca. Real items would let La Botella (agave) move to the top row, next to El Cantarito, and would fill El Barril's empty foot.

Rewrite the wine, beer and spirits lines as short sourced guest sentences instead of 'X · style' tags, for example 'Dry, sparkling rosé.' or 'Crisp, pale Czech-style lager on draft.', and drop 'poured straight' so the whole menu speaks in the cocktails' voice.
Replace the repeated bilingual subheads (AGAVE · Agave, BRANDY · Brandy) with a Spanish-only label or a real translation pair, and ask the Coordinator to approve COÑAC for the Brandy sub.
Ask the Coordinator whether Brut Rosé is sold by the glass or the bottle (the draft label is empty), then print 'copa' or 'botella' so every wine price is labelled.
Put the venue's own name in the masthead (needs input) so the loteria tabla belongs to this cantina rather than a generic 'Cantina & Cocktail Bar'.

fixes: Give every price in a mixed card a pour label, or leave them all unlabelled: in La Rosa, Brut Rosé 13 sits unlabelled under two 'copa' prices, so print 'copa' or 'botella' once the venue answers needs_input 5, and meanwhile send the designer a layout note to reserve the label slot so the 13 lines up with the 12 and 11.

Make the cocktail descriptions use one lead grammar: the Margarita should lead with its sourced method like the other three ('Shaken: tequila blanco, fresh lime, orange liqueur and agave syrup; bright and citrus-forward.' from recipe_versions f06abb74 method and the draft desc).

Layout note for the designer: set the description measure so lines break at a phrase and not at half width. The Daiquiri's 'fresh lime and / house demerara syrup' and the Old Fashioned's 'demerara / syrup' breaks look ragged next to the full-width Margarita lines, so use one consistent measure (about 44 characters) with no single word carried onto a line.

Rewrite the spirits and wine lines so they don't just repeat the item name: use the one extra sourced fact available (for example 'Unaged, poured straight.' only if beverage_categories 04d72e1f gains a note; otherwise shorten to 'Poured straight.'), and for wine drop the name echo so it reads just 'Dry red' / 'Dry white'.

Fill or tighten El Barril's roughly 60 pt dead zone between Dry Cider and the foot rule, either with real venue items (needs_input 7: Mexican lager, agua fresca) or by rebalancing the rows, so the prices in the beer card don't look stranded above empty paper in print.

lens: descriptions and prices laid out together on preview-phone.png (Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar, Iowa City)
top_problem: On the phone, half the list has no real description. The wine and spirits lines mostly repeat the item name as a tag ('Malbec · Malbec · dry red', 'Pinot Grigio · Pinot Grigio · dry white', 'Brut Rosé · Brut rosé · dry sparkling', 'Blanco Tequila · Tequila blanco, poured straight.', 'Cognac VSOP · Cognac VSOP, poured straight.'), which is an automatic-fail pattern for criterion 12. Brut Rosé 13 and all three spirits also print prices with no serve label, while Malbec and Pinot Grigio carry 'copa'. Every printed fact checks out: the Margarita is Rocks with a lime wheel, the Manhattan is a Coupe with a cocktail cherry, the House Daiquiri is a Coupe with a lime coin and 'Shake with ice and fine strain', and the Brown Butter Old Fashioned is Rocks with an orange peel and 'Stir with ice and strain over a large cube'. The Manhattan leaves out the bitters because the draft sets public_components {aromatic-bitters:false}, which is correct. All 14 prices match the draft doc and phg.menu_items.menu_price.
fixes: Replace the name-echo tags with guest-language lines built only from the draft's own words: Malbec 'Dry red wine.', Pinot Grigio 'Dry white wine.', Brut Rosé 'Dry sparkling rosé.' (draft desc for each item), and for the spirits lead with the draft's 'Straight pours by category.' as one card-level line instead of repeating 'X, poured straight.' under every name.

Label every non-cocktail price in one system: 'copa' also on Brut Rosé 13 if it is by the glass, and a pour label on the spirits (for example 'pour'), or add needs_input for the pour size. Right now two wines are labelled and four prices are not.

Remove the redundant doubled subheads 'AGAVE · Agave' and 'BRANDY · Brandy' by printing the Spanish word once (or using 'AGAVE' alone), so the Spanish/English pattern stays meaningful and doesn't read as taxonomy.

For venue fit, flag in needs_input that a Mexican cantina showing two tequilas, no mezcal, no Mexican lager and a Czech Pilsner first on draft undersells the concept. Do not invent items; ask the venue for its agave and Mexican beer list and whether the Margarita should lead with more emphasis.

On the phone, raise the italic serve-cue lines (grey, smallest text on the card) to at least the description size or darken them to full ink, so 'On the rocks, lime wheel.' stays readable at 390 px width and does not look like a separate orphaned line.
